acceptance: T1 Positive recovery: actual MCP/service recovery into a second clean worktree and an independent URL-matching clone succeeds after the original checkout path is unavailable; subsequent readiness/prepare/advance/final validation use the new path; prepared receipts remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

T2 Negative recovery: wrong owner/generation/epoch/path/head, incomplete relocation tuple, dirty destination, wrong branch/repository, missing history and stale CAS all refuse without publishing any partial ownership/path change. A simulated retry-time destination mutation is revalidated. Completed/aborted batches and prohibited late moves retain their existing refusals.

T3 Idempotency and partial closeout: exact retry adds no transition; same new generation with a different tuple/reason refuses; old owner writes fail. After one member is done, an active batch can relocate at unchanged integration_head/final_pr and finish remaining members with fresh new-path evidence. Finished receipts/evidence and historical paths/epochs are unchanged; relocation grants no advance, reprepare or rebind rights; copied old-location success cannot pass.

T4 Capability: initialize and batch-show expose the same additive relocation feature from the installed runtime; absent feature is distinguishable from support. Legacy same-path owner recovery remains usable. No store or receipt migration occurs on ordinary operations or upgrade.

T5 CLI freshness: an actual show command reads a field larger than its budget through all --rev continuations; the concatenated content is exact. Moved revision refuses/restarts rather than mixing pages; offline/cache output remains explicitly stale without authoritative rev.

T6 PRE-TAG release rubric: failing-before/passing-after recovery/pagination regressions and existing lifecycle invariants pass. Candidate-installed scratch MCP lifecycle actually exercises bootstrap/create/take/renew/finish, conflict and offline publication paths. A real read-only floor CLI command also succeeds against an existing real downstream store from its normal consumer session; neither isolated smoke nor permanent BenchBox adoption substitutes for this gate. Record both results BEFORE tag; failure blocks publication, never becomes a follow-up.

T7 Documentation and delivery: ADR 0012, API/CLI/capability/recovery/release notes describe the guarded exception and trust limit; both consumers pin the same approved catalog revision. One runtime PR including the supported GitHub-only publication path merges through required gates. Only after T6 passes is its merged revision tagged/released with wheel/sdist/SHA256SUMS; PyPI requires separate explicit opt-in and no PyPI publisher starts in this release.

T8 Released-byte proof: install the exact released wheel in an isolated environment, verify it against release checksums, run initialize and read-only/scratch-store recovery/CLI smoke without sibling-source imports, and record tag/source revision/asset hashes/results. Do not activate BenchBox or wait for its downstream item here.

T9 Publication and recovery boundaries: verify the actual GitHub release workflow publishes the approved assets while PyPI is ineligible/skipped without relying on credentials or failed execution. Recovery instructions contain no tokenless-abort fallback; private expected-token recovery/new-token persistence are explicit, and absent prerequisites are reported without exposing raw registry material. No additional PR, soak or store migration is introduced.
